name: Compositor & Window Manager
shortDesc: The core graphical engine responsible for tiling, drawing window frames, animations, and hotkeys.
detailedDesc: Under Wayland, the compositor is both the display server and the window manager. It coordinates GPU buffers and manages workspaces.

phase.title: Base & Architecture
phase.description: Core display server protocols, desktop architecture paradigms, and package manager helpers.

packages.name: Hyprland (Recommended)
packages.description: Dynamic tiling Wayland compositor featuring smooth bezier animations, Kawase blur, rounded corners, and powerful IPC sockets.
cons: Rapid development pace requires keeping plugins in sync with updates

packages.name: Sway
packages.description: Drop-in i3-compatible Wayland compositor built directly on wlroots. Minimalist, rock-solid, and battle-tested.
cons: No built-in blur or advanced rounded window shaders (requires forks)

packages.name: Niri
packages.description: Scrollable-tiling Wayland compositor inspired by PaperWM. Windows open in infinite horizontal ribbons.
cons: Different paradigm than standard grid tiling WMs

packages.name: River
packages.description: Dynamic tiling Wayland compositor following the Suckless and dwm philosophy. Highly scriptable via IPC.
cons: Requires external layout generators for custom arrangements

packages.name: Labwc
packages.description: Openbox-like stacking Wayland compositor focusing on simplicity and lightweight efficiency.
pros: Great for classic floating window lovers
cons: Not primarily designed for automated keyboard tiling
